about: SL-001, O-018: the class 'member-name clashes inside MainWindow'. MainWindow is a partial class: its XAML generates one field per x:Name, and its code-behind declares members, in a namespace that holds the App's other types. Three ways a name is produced twice by accident, each a compile error or a silent hiding. x-name-member-clash: an x:Name and a member the code-behind declares share a name (the generated field and the member, CS0102). member-kind-clash: a method and a property, field or event of the code-behind share a name (CS0102), where overloaded methods do not. x-name-hides-type: an x:Name is also the name of a type of the App's namespace, so inside MainWindow the generated field hides the type and a call through the type name does not compile (the design's first pure class, CoverageText, against its TextBlock). 'expect' is the list of '<rule>:<name>' the checker must report for the row, in order of rule then name, and empty for a row that must stay quiet. The first two rows are the design's own names before the fix (a class CoverageText beside a TextBlock named CoverageText; a property Coverage beside the static method Coverage), which is the code before the fix failing the rows it is claimed to close.

rows.name: the design's first pure class beside a TextBlock of that name
the design's internal Coverage property beside the static Coverage method
a method named like a generated field
a property named like a generated field
a field named like a generated field, with a tuple type
an event beside a method of its name
a nested type named like a generated field
the fix: CoveragePanelText and a CoverageLines TextBlock, a CoverageModel property beside the Coverage method
overloads of one method are one kind
an x:Name inside a template is a name in that template, not a field of the window
